activity_context.topic_title: The Dimension of the Null Space of a Matrix

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Nullity of a Matrix Using Row Reduction
examples.worked_solution:
To find $\textrm{dim}(\textrm{Null}(A))$, we reduce $A$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & -3 & -2 & -1 \\ -6 & 0 & -7 & 4 \\ 0 & 9 & 6 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & -3 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 9 & 6 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & -3 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 9 & 6 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & -3 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix has $3$ pivot columns and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $3$rd column). 

Therefore,

$$
\textrm{nullity}(A) = \textrm{dim}(\textrm{Null}(A)) = 1.
$$

feedback.problem:
Which of the following statements are true?

- If $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$ then $\text{dim(Null}(A))=2.$
- If $B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & \,0\end{aligned}]$ then $\text{dim(Null}(B))=1.$
- If $C=[\begin{aligned}5 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$ then $\text{dim(Null}(C))=0.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The dimension of the null space of a matrix is the number of non-pivot columns in the matrix. 

Also, all of the given matrices are in row echelon form.

With that in mind, let's consider each of the statements.

- Statement I is false. The matrix $A$ has $2$ pivot columns and no non-pivot columns. So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(A))=0.
$$

- Statement II is true. The matrix $B$ has $2$ pivot columns and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $3$rd column). So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(B))=1.
$$

- Statement III is true. The matrix $C$ has $3$ pivot columns and no non-pivot columns. So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(C))=0.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
